questions.question: In C++20, which feature allows compile-time string manipulation?
questions.explanation: consteval forces a function to always produce a compile-time result, enabling compile-time string manipulation.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of std::sort on average?
questions.explanation: std::sort uses Introsort which has O(n log n) average and worst-case complexity.

questions.question: Which smart pointer owns a uniquely owned resource in C++?
questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr provides exclusive ownership of a dynamically allocated object.

questions.question: What does RAII stand for in C++?
questions.explanation: RAII binds resource lifetime to object lifetime — acquisition in constructor, release in destructor.

questions.question: In C++11, what does noexcept indicate?
options: The function may throw but is optimized
questions.explanation: noexcept specifies that a function will not throw exceptions; if it does, std::terminate is called.

questions.question: Which virtual function feature enables runtime polymorphism in C++?
questions.explanation: The vtable (virtual table) holds function pointers for dynamic dispatch of virtual functions.
